title: Running Twice as Fast Just to Stay in Place: The Red Queen Trap
alt_title_1: Leigh Van Valen's 1973 Law Applied to Modern Careers
alt_title_2: How to Escape Commodity Competition With Two-Domain Skills
description_hook: In 1973, evolutionary biologist Leigh Van Valen formulated the Red Queen Hypothesis to explain why species can evolve nonstop without gaining any survival edge. Here is how the exact same trap stalls single-skill careers.

affiliate_cta.offer_name: Two-Domain Career Moat Map + Evolutionary Strategy Reading List
affiliate_cta.pinned_comment: What two separate domains could you combine so you stop competing on price or speed alone? 👇 Grab our Two-Domain Career Moat Map + reading list here: https://kenvh0010-lang.github.io/admin/bio/

scenes.headline: Working Harder Every Year for Zero Extra Leverage
scenes.stat_label: WHEN FASTER OUTPUT ONLY MATCHES THE CROWD
bullets: Everyone adopts the same AI prompts and resume keywords
Hours climb while bargaining power stays flat
scenes.narration: Why can you work harder every single year, adopt every new productivity tool, and still watch your career leverage stand completely still?
scenes.source: Leigh Van Valen, 'A New Evolutionary Law', Evolutionary Theory (1973)

scenes.headline: Leigh Van Valen's 1973 Red Queen Hypothesis
bullets: Predator and prey upgrades cancel each other's relative edge
Constant sprinting is required merely to avoid falling behind
scenes.narration: In 1973, evolutionary biologist Leigh Van Valen proposed the Red Queen Hypothesis: when rivals compete inside the exact same niche, every adaptation gets matched, forcing nonstop sprinting just to survive.
scenes.source: Leigh Van Valen, Evolutionary Theory, Vol. 1, pp. 1-30 (1973)

scenes.headline: Commodity Single-Lane Races Compress Margins
scenes.left_body: 10,000 peers with identical templates -> faster work, lower pay
scenes.right_body: Technical craft + domain strategy -> scarce intersection of one
scenes.narration: Competing on one standardized skill puts you in a commodity tournament. When ten thousand peers use identical templates and AI prompts, faster output only lowers everyone's rate.

scenes.headline: Pair Orthogonal Skills to Exit the Tournament
scenes.stat_subtext: Hard craft + rare communication or domain fluency -> zero clones
scenes.narration: Escape the single-lane race through orthogonal skill pairing: combine a hard technical craft with persuasive writing, client strategy, or domain regulation that rivals ignore.
scenes.source: Applied from Van Valen (1973) & Scott Adams, How to Fail at Almost Everything (2013)

scenes.headline: Step Sideways Out of Crowded Tournaments
scenes.stat_label: CHANGE THE GAME INSTEAD OF DOUBLING SPEED
bullets: Never fight a head-on commodity war you can sidestep
Build at the bridge between two valuable worlds
scenes.narration: Stop running faster down a crowded lane; step sideways into an intersection almost nobody else occupies.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule of thumb (advice, not a study)
